resources.name: C# surface
resources.description: The C# surface Lamella supports: types, BCL, GPIO.
resources.text:
# Lamella C# surface -- what you can write today

Lamella runs a subset of C# on a small embedded interpreter. A program is a full C# program with a `Main`.
Use `lamella_check` to compile-check without running, and `lamella_run` to run on the host interpreter.

## Supported today
- **Types**: `int`, `long`, `uint`, `byte`, `bool`, `char`, `string`, `double`/`float`, arrays (`int[]`, `T[]`),
  user `class` / `struct`, `enum`.
- **Control flow**: `if`/`else`, `for`, `while`, `do`, `foreach` (over arrays), `switch`, methods, recursion.
- **Console**: `System.Console.Write` / `WriteLine` (strings + numerics). `ReadLine` is host-REPL only.
- **Math**: `System.Math` (`Abs`, `Min`, `Max`, `Sqrt`, `Pow`, `Floor`, ...).
- **String**: concatenation (`+`), `.Length`, indexing, `.Substring`, `.ToString()`, `$"..."` interpolation.
- **Operators**: arithmetic, comparison, logical, bitwise, shifts.

## NOT available yet -- these are compile errors
- `List<T>`, `Dictionary<,>`, LINQ, `StringBuilder`, most of `System.Collections` / `System.Linq`.
- `async` / `await`, `Task`, threads (host-side only).
- File / network I/O.

The corlib surface is growing -- when in doubt, write it and run `lamella_check`; the diagnostics tell you what
is missing. Prefer plain loops + arrays over collections.

## Hardware (GPIO) -- for `deploy` / `run_on_device`
Use the Microsoft **`System.Device.Gpio`** API (namespace `System.Device.Gpio`, NOT `System.Devices`):

```csharp
using System.Device.Gpio;
var gpio = new GpioController();
gpio.OpenPin(25, PinMode.Output);
gpio.Write(25, PinValue.High);
```

Pin numbers are board-specific -- see the `lamella://boards` resource. A full blink is in
`lamella://samples/blink`.

## Workflow
1. `lamella_check` -> fix errors fast (no run).
2. `lamella_run` -> run on the host interpreter (no board).
3. `lamella_list_devices` -> see attached boards; `lamella_identify_device` -> confirm which one.
4. `lamella_run_on_device` (transient) or `lamella_deploy` (persistent) -> run on real silicon.
5. `lamella_debug_launch` + breakpoints/step/stack -> source-level debug on the board.

# Supported dev boards

The `board_model` wire values a board reports over Lamella Link:

| model | board |
|--:|---|
| 0 | custom board |
| 1 | BBC micro:bit v1 |
| 2 | Raspberry Pi Pico 2 |
| 3 | SAM4S Xplained Pro |
| 4 | SAM E54 Xplained Pro |
| 5 | SAMD21 Xplained Pro |
| 6 | ATSAMW25 Xplained Pro |
| 7 | STM32F091 Nucleo-64 |
| 8 | STM32L476 Nucleo |
| 9 | Arduino MKR1000 |
| 10 | Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W |
| 11 | BBC micro:bit v2 |
| 12 | Arduino Zero |
| 13 | Raspberry Pi Pico |
| 14 | Espressif ESP32-C6 |
| 15 | Arduino Due |
| 16 | Adafruit Feather M0 Express |
| 17 | Adafruit Feather M0 WiFi |
| 18 | Adafruit Feather RP2040 Adalogger |

resources.name: Supported chips
resources.description: The silicon registry: chip families by SW-DP IDCODE, cores, RAM/flash.
resources.text:
# Supported silicon (by SW-DP IDCODE)

- **Raspberry Pi RP2350** (`rp2350`) -- core dual Cortex-M33 / Hazard3 RISC-V, IDCODE 0x4c013477, 520 KB RAM, flash {"kind":"external-qspi"} -- Flash is EXTERNAL QSPI; package/GPIO is not a register -- from the board, not the silicon.
- **Nordic Semiconductor nRF51** (`nrf51`) -- core Cortex-M0, IDCODE 0x0bb11477, flash {"pageSizeReg":268435472,"pageCountReg":268435476,"decode":"pageSize*pageCount"}
- **Microchip SAM D21** (`samd21`) -- core Cortex-M0+, IDCODE 0x0bc11477 -- The ATSAMW25 = SAMD21G18 (48-pin) + ATWINC1500 Wi-Fi; the specific SKU is in the DSU DID DEVSEL field.
- **Nordic Semiconductor nRF52833** (`nrf52833`) -- core Cortex-M4F, IDCODE 0x2ba01477, 128 KB RAM, flash {"pageSizeReg":268435472,"pageCountReg":268435476,"decode":"pageSize*pageCount"} -- BBC micro:bit v2 / v2.1. Cortex-M4F -> shares the 0x2ba01477 DPIDR with STM32 M3/M4 -> ID by the FICR device-id. [idcode runtime-verified; FICR regs + flash size bench-verify.]
- **STMicroelectronics STM32F0 (F091)** (`stm32f0`) -- core Cortex-M0, IDCODE 0x0bb11477, flash {"sizeReg":536868812,"unit":"KB","note":"STM32F0 flash-size register (u16, KB)"} -- STM32F091 Nucleo-64 = STM32F091RCT6 (256 KB flash, 32 KB SRAM). Shares the Cortex-M0 DPIDR with the nRF51 -> identify by the DBGMCU device-id.
- **Raspberry Pi RP2040** (`rp2040`) -- core dual Cortex-M0+, IDCODE 0x0bc12477, 264 KB RAM, flash {"kind":"external-qspi"} -- Raspberry Pi Pico / Pico H (board_model 13). External QSPI + a stage-2 boot2 at offset 0 (unlike the RP2350, which scans a PICOBIN block). Browser flasher: UF2 blocks MUST be full 256-byte pages -- a short final block leaves the board stuck in BOOTSEL (runtime-sam4s).
- **WCH (Nanjing Qinheng) CH32V003** (`ch32v003`) -- core RISC-V RV32EC (QingKe, no M-extension -> soft mul/div), IDCODE 0x00000000, 2 KB RAM, flash {"kind":"internal","sizeKb":16,"start":134217728} -- The ~$0.10-0.15 RISC-V MCU. QingKe RV32EC (x0-x15, no M-extension). Debug + flash over the WCH single-wire via a WCH-LinkE (riscvchip 0x09, code flash @ 0x08000000) -- NOT ARM SWD, NOT the Lamella Link serve; deploy/debug = lamella-wch-link + RV32EC AOT (C# compiled to native RV32EC).
- **Espressif ESP32-C6** (`esp32c6`) -- core RISC-V RV32IMAC (HP core) + RV32IMAC (LP core), IDCODE 0x00000000, 512 KB RAM, flash {"kind":"external-qspi"} -- Espressif RISC-V (RV32IMAC), Wi-Fi 6 + BLE 5 + 802.15.4. Serves Lamella Link (board_model 14) over its BUILT-IN USB-Serial-JTAG (VID 303a; SerialTransport holds DTR/RTS low, else a host RESET wipes a RAM serve). Not ARM SWD.
